issues.description: The solution's toString method is declared with return type Object (public Object toString()) while the language and the exercise expect to override Object.toString(), which has return type String. The @Override annotation combined with an Object return type is invalid and will cause a compilation error and confusion for students expecting to implement/override toString() as a String-returning method.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the toString method signature in the solution (and ensure the template/example shows the same) to public String toString() and return a String. Keep the @Override annotation so the method properly overrides java.lang.Object.toString().
